1.explanation:
- parsefiguredivs.lua identifies and splits a multi-column figure block into separate sub-figure divs, but only tags them as subfloats when an explicit ID is present.
- floats.lua carries the general float processing logic; it determines whether to emit a Pandoc native figure or a raw LaTeX minipage/caption sequence.
- figures.lua (common) builds the actual caption nodes; it currently falls back to full captions unless a subfigure ID is applied.
- crossref/figures.lua handles cross-reference IDs and chooses between `\caption` and `\subcaption`, again keyed off the presence of labels.
- fig-cleanup.lua (quarto-post) tidies up the final figure AST, but it assumes that the earlier stages already chose the correct caption type.

To fix the bug, these filters need to be updated to recognize any multi-column/subfigure grouping — even if unlabeled — and emit `\subcaption{…}` for each panel under the group’s main caption.
1.bug_scenario: When users create a multi-column figure (`::: {#fig-elephants layout-ncol="2"}`) with two images but do not explicitly supply subfigure IDs (e.g. `{#fig-surus}`), Quarto’s PDF/LaTeX pipeline treats each subimage as an independent full figure: it emits `\caption{…}` in each minipage rather than `\subcaption{…}`. In the final document the two panels get numbered as separate “Figure 1” and “Figure 2” instead of (a)/(b) under a shared “Figure 1.” In contrast, once you add explicit IDs, Quarto switches to `\subcaption{…}` and you get the intended subfigure labeling. The bug is that Quarto fails to detect and render unlabeled subfloats as subcaptions automatically.

2.explanation:
All of the listed files participate in turning a multi-column figure block into LaTeX code with proper subfigures:  

• resources/filters/quarto-pre/parsefiguredivs.lua  
  Splits a figure div into individual image blocks (subfloats) and records any IDs.  Without IDs, subfloats aren’t flagged for subcaption output.  

• resources/filters/layout/figures.lua  
  Lays out subfloats in a minipage grid and chooses between \caption vs. \subcaption based on whether filters have marked them as subfigures.  

• resources/filters/common/figures.lua  
  Contains shared helper logic (e.g. detecting figure vs. subfigure, pulling IDs) which currently only recognizes explicit IDs for subcaption mode.  

• resources/filters/crossref/figures.lua  
  Handles cross-reference labels for figure and subfigure IDs.  It only generates \subcaption labels when an image carries an explicit ID.  

• src/render/output-tex.ts  
  The TypeScript Pandoc output driver emits raw LaTeX for figures.  It currently generates plain \caption calls for every image when IDs are missing instead of falling back to auto-numbered subcaptions.  

To fix this bug, the code in these files must be updated so that any multi-column figure without explicit image IDs still gets rendered with \subcaption instead of \caption, and that cross-reference labels are autogenerated (a), (b), etc., even when users omit IDs on the subfloats.
2.bug_scenario: When a user places multiple images side-by-side in a PDF output container in Quarto without giving each image a cross-reference ID, Quarto’s LaTeX generation logic treats each image as a separate top-level figure rather than as sub-figures. In the unlabeled case we get two full \caption calls ("Figure 1: Surus", "Figure 2: Hanno") under one \begin{figure}…\end{figure}, instead of a single figure with two subcaptions ("(a) Surus", “(b) Hanno"). By contrast, when explicit IDs are provided on the images (e.g. {#fig-surus}), Quarto emits \subcaption commands correctly. The root cause is that the filters and output code only switch into “subfigure” mode if individual image blocks carry an ID, so unlabeled subfloats fall back to plain captions.
